  "screen_rationale": "The study compares preclinical cardiac electrophysiology data (in vitro and in vivo) against clinical QT effects and torsade de pointes reports for 100 drugs, calculating margins between therapeutic plasma concentrations and hERG IC50 values. This directly quantifies the agreement between animal model predictions and human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "Published data on hERG (or IKr ) activity, cardiac action potential duration (at 90% repolarisation; APD 90 ), and QT prolongation in dogs were compared against QT effects and reports of TdP in humans for 100 drugs.",

    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on cardiac electrophysiology, QT interval prolongation, and torsade de pointes, all of which are cardiovascular endpoints.",
  "model_type": "in-vitro-or-in-silico-comparator",
  "model_evidence": "Published data on hERG (or IKr ) activity, cardiac action potential duration (at 90% repolarisation; APD 90 ), and QT prolongation in dogs were compared against QT effects and reports of TdP in humans for 100 drugs.",
  "species": [
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "QT prolongation in dogs were compared against QT effects and reports of TdP in humans for 100 drugs.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study compares preclinical data (hERG activity, APD90, QT prolongation in dogs) with clinical outcomes (QT effects, TdP reports in humans), encompassing both biomarker-like measures (QT prolongation) and hard outcomes (torsade de pointes)."
